So I've tossed a few back tonight and I'm feeling... social. Why not seed a sub I want so badly to see grow with a few of my own favorite recipes? Why, not. Let's bust out the ol' trusty tablet there and get my app going. I'm doing my best here to keep formatting and flow as easy on the eyes and identifiable as possible, so bear with me.

Erm, standard abbreviations abound: LA - LorAnn Oils, TFA - The Flavor Apprentice, SM - Seedman's, FA - FlavourArt, FW - FlavorWest, CAP - Capella Flavors.

Alright, here we go.

Trail Mix

5% Pecan (LA)

5% Black Walnut (LA)

5% Coconut (TFA) -or- 2% Coconut (FA)

2% Toasted Almond (CAP)

2.5% Hazelnut V2 (CAP)

Ethyl Maltol to taste. (I prefer 1 drop per 2ml)

Notes on Trail Mix: this had a long road behind it. At one time I called it "Deez." Geddit? Deez Nuts. Heh. So the idea here was to get a good, slightly complex nutty vape without using peanut butter or peanut vapes of any kind. I ran out of TFA Coconut the day my first bottle of FA Coconut arrived, and I've never looked back. Even at 2%, it's slightly stronger than I really, really wanted - but good enough for gub'ment work. The Ethyl Maltol doesn't really do a whole lot unless you let it sit and stew for a few good, hot days. All in the mind, though. All in the mind. Anywho, there's Trail Mix. Next up...

Applegranete Crisp

10% Apple (LA)

4% Pomegranate (LA)

10% Biscotti (FW)

So there's that one. Admittedly, I wasn't keen on this at first. It felt a bit too "fruity" for me, and the biscotti was still almost non-existent even at a whoppin' ten percent. But that's all the name of the game when you're testing out new combinations and finding new flavors, right? Take the good with the bad. Give it a week later, I checked it out to see how it was maturing and was really quite happy with it. There's a certain bready feel to it and the two fruits toned down a bit. I liked it, enough to make up a bigger bottle that got the wife's attention. Now it's hers, and I promised her I'd share it.

Got a few others, some one-off's that were mighty tasty. Nothing super complex or complicated, but can't beat a good tasting vape.

Frozen Sprite

5% Lemon Lime (FA)

1% Citrus Punch (FA)

0.001% Koolada

Just a smidge gives this a nice cold snap to go with it. Citrus Punch gives it a very, very mellow orange-lemon pop that makes it a little different than regular old Lemon Lime. This'll gunk up your coils fast as hell, though. And don't vape it too high, I find I have to turn the wattage on any-damned-thing I use this one all the way down or I'm burning it up.

White Peach Yogurt

2.5% Yogurt (FA)

2% White Peach (FA)

This is straight out deliciousness in a bottle. And the Yogurt's got a bunch of shit that'll cause popcorn lung if you vape it for fifty years non stop. I can't do this all day, or even very often, but when I do it's a danggum treat. Can't believe how identifiably Yogurt it is, and the White Peach is a slightly sweeter, candy-ish Peach that makes this straight up comparable to a cup of Dannon.

Sour Apple Chewing Gum

10% Granny Smith Apple (TFA)

12% Wintergreen (TFA)

Koolada to taste (it's Koolada, good luck.)

Another one of those "I wonder how this would taste?" moment that was interesting but not good enough to make it into my regular rotation. The Wintergreen makes this almost a dead-ringer for... I want to say Trident? Who out there makes a Sour Apple chewing gum? It's that. If you've ever had that, that's what this tastes like.

Berry-Nilla Coldsnap

3% Blackberry (TFA)

2% Black Cherry (TFA)

4% Strawberry (TFA)

6% Vanilla Swirl (TFA)

Koolada to taste

This is another one that takes about a week to taste awesome. And it does, too! The Strawberry is right up front when it's fresh, but it'll subside and the Vanilla Swirl will kind of mask everything a bit. Almost ends up tasting frosty and creamy at the same time. Fruity and sweet.

Alright, one more. Another fave, all-day vape, but simple.

Perique 'n Pipe

4% Perique Black (FA)

6% Coumarin Pipe Tobacco (FW)

Ethyl Maltol to taste

I'm not going to lie to you, reader. You've stuck with me this long, you deserve more. You can't barely taste any damned Coumarin in there at all. In fact, you have to crank that sumbitch up to about 15-16% to even get a hint. It's that light. But it works well with the Perique, which if you've ever had a whiff of you'd know is quite high in peppery, earthy notes. The Coumarin smooths it out a bit and adds kind of a lifeless, tasteless half-body zombie flavor type thing. It's not my absolute favorite, but I do enjoy vaping it. Why, you ask? It's a mindless vape. It's something to vape while I drive or write or drink or hike. It isn't all up in my face, there's a subtle taste, but it's just... decent.

So there you have you crazy people. Have at em and go make money off it, or experiment with them, or make them and send me a message two weeks from now telling me how shitty it tastes.

You know what you should do? You should post here more often! Yes, you, reading this! Post something! We need to get this place a rip-roarin'.

Peace and chicken grease fellow DIY'ers. Here's to you.

Both the TFA Greek and the FA Yogurt, both of those are in my arsenal. I'll definitely agree with you there, the Greek is my preference through and through. I remember popping the top cap of that bad boy for the first time, I couldn't believe someone would find it palatable with as sour as it smelled. "With a smell like that, it must taste good," I figured. Just like bleu cheese - the smell turns most off, but that taste is delicious. FA Yogurt is good, and it still blows me away at how accurately it conveys the actual yogurt-ness of yogurt. But Greek? Throw some one-off fruits at it, maybe a little nutty something to follow, that's going to be a good vape.

I think there's a big push to associate mixing juices with chemistry, and for all sales and professional aspects I can definitely agree with that. Cleanliness isn't just next to Godliness, it's the only decent way to approach making something consumable for another human being. That being said, I can't help but associate it with cooking more. To me, in my podunk little garage, opening my flavoring case is no different than opening my pantry, standing back and going, "What's gonna work here?" And I can work it. I like to think it's a smidge of a talent, but I love cooking. Never did it as a profession, I was always in home construction, framing, landscaping etc. But it's my super secret passion that I enjoy. When it clicked in my head that that's all mixing juice was, there's just no going back. I can't just go order out every night, that's more or less depriving me of a hobby.

So, all that being said. I've been known to make funky bottles. It's a little like my freestyle. Most of my old stock is in dripper bottles, most of my newer flavorings need a needle or pipette. So I'll "cook." Not all the time, not as a regular rule or anything, just as kind of a reward for getting my "mix" list done. The fun part.

I amped myself up, made a tiny little single-flavoring order for FA Lemon Sicily and it took like three days to get here. ...yeah. :/
